one_line: AI financing surges, Google pressures schools, and safety agencies warn of AI‑driven threats.

themes.title: AI infrastructure financing expands
themes.text: Goldman Sachs and Apollo are seeking investors for up to $500 million slices of SpaceX’s $40 billion GPU debt. AMD recorded a $1.1 billion non‑cash charge tied to AI chip warrants with OpenAI and Meta, while Qualcomm aims for $5 billion in AI data‑center revenue in fiscal 2027. TeraWulf secured a Google credit backstop for a Kentucky data‑center project linked to $19 billion of Anthropic lease commitments.

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs and Apollo seek investors for up to $500 M slices of SpaceX’s $40 B chip financing
AMD records $1.1 billion non‑cash charge from OpenAI, Meta AI chip warrants
Qualcomm aims for $5 billion in AI data‑center revenue in fiscal 2027
TeraWulf secures Google credit backstop for Anthropic Kentucky data center project

themes.title: Google forces AI in school search
themes.text: Google announced that K‑12 administrators can disable Gemini and related AI tools, but schools that block AI will lose access to Google Search, which will always include AI Mode and AI Overviews. The policy will take effect next year and has drawn criticism from educators.

stories.headline: Google lets schools disable Gemini but forces AI in Search
Google will cut search access for schools that reject its AI tools

themes.title: AI misuse triggers safety alerts
themes.text: Pangram released Image 1.0 and Image Flash 1.0 models claiming over 99% detection of AI‑generated images. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre warned banks, NBFCs and fintech firms that attackers are using AI agents to compromise systems and execute multi‑crore fraudulent transactions, urging implementation of CERT‑In advisories and transaction limits.

stories.headline: Pangram launches Image 1.0 and Image Flash 1.0 AI detection models
India's cyber agency warns banks and fintechs of AI-driven fraud attacks
I4C warns Indian banks and fintechs of AI‑led cyberattacks
